# FLX-3305: a declaration is accepted but not generated and coverage is strict

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

A contract can declare what this version of the engine accepts and does not generate: a relationship's sharedColumns, a column's sharedAttribute, and a check that determines no column (one without a generates setting, or one of a form that setting does not reach), alone or reading another row through a relationship. The rows are drawn as if the declaration were not there, so some of them can break it. That is reported on every plan and listed under What Was Not Proven in the evidence report; under --strict-coverage, or when the Simulation declares strictCoverage: true under its com.agentics.flux/1 extensions, it is refused, before any row exists, with one table row per declaration. To have a check generated, give a derive or a dependency for the column it constrains, or set generates on a check that is a difference of dates over the row's own columns. Kernel 0.2.0 copies a sharedColumns or sharedAttribute declaration into a column that is neither a key nor a foreign key, in an emit generated from statistics, when the Simulation declares copies: true, and generates a rule that reads another row through a relationship; kernel 0.1.0 does neither, and a key or foreign key is never copied. What is left can only be removed from the bundle or accepted. Or drop --strict-coverage, and strictCoverage from the Simulation if it declares it, to accept the declaration as it is.
